name: Refused
label: Epitaph
lede: Refused ended in 1998 with police shutting down a basement show in Virginia and a written promise never to play together again. They kept it for 14 years, then turned up at Coachella.

eras.title: Four kids, a Swedish university town, one 7-inch to make
eras.text: Refused start in early 1991 in Umeå, a university town in northern Sweden, with a modest plan: play outside town and put out a 7-inch. Straight edge, vegan and loudly political, they grow up inside a tiny local scene that ends up feeding a lot of Swedish hardcore.

years.h: [[Dennis Lyxzén|d7bb37a5-3d48-4a2f-a761-fe66d5cdb409]] and [[David Sandström|61d60747-57f2-42c2-b728-c6f097869a81]] start a band in Umeå
years.p: Guitarist Pär Hansson and bassist Jonas Lindgren fill out the first lineup. The plan is small: get out of town and put out a 7-inch.
years.xp:
Wikipedia puts the start in early 1991, with Lyxzén on vocals and Sandström on drums. The early records came out on small Swedish hardcore labels.

Lyxzén and Sandström are the two constants. They are there for every phase of the band, from the first 7-inch plans to the 2025 farewell.

eras.title: Screaming replaces shouting, and Victory comes aboard
eras.text: The debut album and a run of EPs make Refused a fixture of European hardcore. By the second album, the vocals are screamed and the guitars lean metal.

years.cap: Dennis Lyxzén at the Hultsfred festival, Sweden, 1994
years.h: Startrec and We Bite release the first album
years.p: Burning Heart is on the credits too, and the Everlasting EP comes out the same year.
play: This Just Might Be... the Truth

years.src: Wikipedia: Songs to Fan the Flames of Discontent
years.h: Songs to Fan the Flames of Discontent brings in the screaming
years.p: Recorded in December 1995 with producer Pelle Gunnerfeldt, it runs 12 songs in 30 minutes and opens with Rather Be Dead.
years.xp:
Wikipedia notes that Lyxzén moves from the shouting of the debut to screamed vocals, with metal all through the guitars.

The title comes from the Industrial Workers of the World's Little Red Songbook, the 1909 collection tied to Joe Hill. It came out through Startrec and We Bite in Europe and Victory Records in the US.
play: Songs to Fan the Flames of Discontent

eras.title: One last record, and hardcore hates it
eras.text: The band decides, privately, that this is the last record, and tries to make one nobody can file under hardcore. It comes out, and hardcore hates it.

years.big: "We did not use Pro Tools at all."
q: We could have called the record Fuck You.
years.src: Louder · Wikipedia: The Shape of Punk to Come
years.h: Recording The Shape of Punk to Come at Tonteknik in Umeå
years.p: Producer Pelle Henricsson, on the late 1997 sessions, cut on 24-track two-inch tape. Jazz, electronics and strings go into the hardcore.
years.xp:
Henricsson has said the album was made on tape and that groove was the guiding word. Lyxzén has said the band was on the brink of collapse and often its own worst enemy.

Louder reports that Sandström pushed for jazz, Brännström for electronics, and Lyxzén for surrealism and Situationist politics, and that the pulling in different directions caused friction.

years.src: Louder · Wikipedia: The Shape of Punk to Come
years.h: The Shape of Punk to Come is released into a breakup
years.p: Burning Heart puts it out on 27 October, subtitled A Chimerical Bombination in 12 Bursts, with New Noise at its center. Reviews and fans split.
years.xp:
"People were kind of pissed off when that record came out," Lyxzén told Louder. Listeners wrote in that if this was the shape of punk to come, they were quitting punk.

Wikipedia calls it a commercial and critical failure at release, with some critics declining to rate it. Kerrang! later put it at No. 13 on its 2003 list of the 50 most influential albums, and it had sold 179,000 copies in the US by June 2015.
play: The Shape of Punk to Come

years.src: Louder · Wikipedia: The Shape of Punk to Come
yt: New Noise, Bielefeld, 1998, on the last tour
years.h: Police end a basement show in Harrisonburg, Virginia
years.p: It is the last US show of the tour, stopped after a few songs. The band announces it is done.
years.xp:
Louder dates the show to 5 October. Another Louder piece puts the split on 6 October, three weeks before the album came out.

The band's statement ended with the promise above, and added that it would not give interviews to stupid reporters.

Wikipedia calls the tour emotionally devastating and puts it at about eight shows.

years.h: The New Noise Theology E.P. comes out anyway
years.p: Burning Heart releases it in late 1998, after the band is already gone.

eras.title: Dead, and getting bigger
eras.text: Refused stay broken up for 14 years. Dennis Lyxzén fronts The (International) Noise Conspiracy, and the band's reputation grows from a cult item into a reference point.

years.h: Lyxzén keeps singing, in The (International) Noise Conspiracy
years.p: [[The (International) Noise Conspiracy|97da5eb3-79a5-4195-b98e-3d10ef946b08]] gives him a stage for political rock while Refused stays dead.

years.h: Refused Are Fucking Dead, filmed by one of the band
years.p: Guitarist [[Kristofer Steen|63064f8f-5d22-4862-b729-11f7dab678b0]] directs the 38-minute film on the final year, released in Scandinavia on 19 April 2006.
years.xp:
The title echoes Born Against Are Fucking Dead, the New York hardcore band's. The film includes live versions of Life Support Addiction, Circlepit, New Noise and Rather Be Dead.

The DVD adds live footage of nearly all of The Shape of Punk to Come and two music videos.

eras.title: The promise breaks at Coachella
eras.text: The band that said it would never play again does exactly that, and the crowds are huge. A new album follows, and so does a firing that gets public.

years.h: Umeå gets the first reunion show, in secret
years.p: Announced for Coachella on 9 January, Refused play their first show since 1998 at home on 29 February, six weeks early.

years.cap: Refused at Coachella, weekend two, 20 April 2012
years.h: The band that swore it was finished plays Coachella twice
years.p: On 13 and 20 April, Refused play their first major reunion shows, 14 years after promising never to play together again.
years.xp:
Wikipedia calls the decision controversial, given the band's original statement.

Europe follows: Groezrock (29 April), Way Out West (9 August), Pukkelpop (18 August), plus Download, Rock am Ring, Hellfest and Roskilde.

years.cap: Refused at Way Out West, Gothenburg, 9 August 2012, on the same tour
years.h: Exel Arena in Umeå closes the 2012 run at home
years.p: On 15 December the tour ends at Exel Arena, with an afterparty at Fabriken the same night.

years.h: Jon Brännström says he was fired with no explanation
years.p: Guitarist [[Jon Brännström|1f9b22d7-4791-4396-8760-7d89ecef0b67]] says on Facebook, on 31 October 2014, that he was let go in 2013. The band says he did not share its passion.
years.xp:
Brännström wrote that he "wasn't given a reasonable explanation and wasn't even invited to sit down and talk about it."

The other members replied: "We cut ties with Jon already in 2013 because he did not share our passion for the band." They also asked why he chose Facebook over a phone call.

Brännström acknowledged that he preferred studio work to touring, but said the dismissal was not mutual.

years.h: Freedom follows a pay-what-you-want single for Nepal relief
years.p: Epitaph releases the first Refused album since 1998 in June, produced by Nick Launay, Shellback and Michael Ilbert. Sessions run in Los Angeles and Stockholm.
years.xp:
The singles came first: Elektra (27 April), Françafrique (26 May) and Dawkins Christ (11 June, premiered on BBC Radio One). The band put out Elektra pay-what-you-want for Save the Children's Nepal earthquake relief.

Recording ran from October 2014 to February 2015. Freedom reached No. 2 in Sweden, No. 18 on the US Top Alternative Albums chart and No. 161 on the Billboard 200.

eras.title: One more record, then goodbye
eras.text: Refused add a bassist and a second guitarist to the core, make one more record, then decide to say goodbye properly.

years.h: War Music is the record fans wanted from Freedom, per Lyxzén
years.p: Sandström and Steen produce it, with drums recorded on Gotland and the rest at Studio Kobra in Stockholm. It is out on 18 October 2019.
years.xp:
A European tour with Thrice followed in autumn 2019 and a North American run with METZ and Youth Code in early 2020.

The band's own statement on the record: "capitalism is cancer and we still believe it can be cured."

years.h: A fictional band called Samurai gets Refused's songs
years.p: Lyxzén sings the songs of Samurai, the band in Cyberpunk 2077, and the game credits them to Refused.
years.xp: Refused recorded the Samurai material in 2019, the same year as War Music.

years.cap: Refused say goodbye to the crowd at the Shrine Auditorium, Los Angeles, 28 March 2025, on the farewell tour
years.h: Refused close at home in Umeå, and the last song is New Noise
years.p: On 21 December 2025 at Kulturväven, a 95-minute set ends a farewell tour of North America and Europe.
years.xp:
The North American leg ran 20 March to 8 April; the European leg ran from 15 June to 11 October.

In September 2025, Lyxzén, [[Magnus Flagge|0fccccce-5646-4267-be8d-90c3358ade4b]] and Sandström announced Backengrillen with saxophonist Mats Gustafsson. Their self-titled debut came out in January 2026.
